Set user preferences.

Stores one or more files in the user's Moodle draft area from plain text, base64, or a remote URL, and returns a draft item id. DO NOT call this function to give files to the user — use create_files instead. This function is only for moving file bytes between storage areas inside Moodle.

Create one or more files and attach them to the conversation for the user to download. Use this when the user asks you to generate a file (CSV, text, code, etc.). The files will appear as downloadable attachments in the chat automatically — do NOT include download links or embed the files in your response text. For creating files to pass to other Moodle tools (e.g. profile picture, forum attachment), use create_draft_file_area instead.

Crop a rectangular region from an image attached to this conversation. Pass the image URL and the crop coordinates (x, y, width, height in pixels). The cropped image is attached to the conversation automatically.
This web service is used to recalculate the value of automatically populated number custom field.
Return guest enrolment instance information.
Validate a guest enrolment password for a course. If correct, stores it as a user preference for future access.
Manually enrol one or more users into courses with specified roles. Supports setting start/end dates and suspended status. The entire operation is atomic (all-or-nothing).
Manual unenrol users
Create meta (course-level linked) enrolment instances. Links a course so that its enrolled users are automatically synced into a meta course. Optionally creates a group in the meta course.
Remove meta (course-level linked) enrolment instances, unlinking courses from a meta course.
Self enrol the current user in the given course.
Get information about a self-enrolment instance, including whether it is active and whether a password is required.

Extract (unzip, unpack, decompress) the files inside an archive or document: .zip, the ZIP-based Office formats (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .odt, .ods, .odp), gzipped tarballs (.tar.gz, .tgz) and Moodle backups (.mbz). The source can be any file on this site: a chat attachment or any pluginfile URL (e.g. a course resource). A single call extracts at most 20 files. Extracted files are attached to the conversation for download automatically — do NOT include download links in your reply.

Read the page currently displayed to the user. LAST RESORT ONLY. Do not call this if the information can come from any other function. Never use it to look up courses, sections, activities, files or users: those come from the Moodle functions, which return the identifiers needed to act on them. Call it only when the request depends on what is rendered on screen and no other function can answer it. It returns no page content itself: the page is saved as a Markdown file that costs a second read_file call to read.

Generate an image using AI based on a text description. The generated image will be attached to the conversation and displayed as a preview automatically — do NOT embed the image or include its URL in your response text. Use this when the user asks you to create, draw, or generate an image.

Converts an ISO 8601 date/time string to a Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch). Use this when you need to convert human-readable dates to timestamps for use with other tools that accept Unix timestamps.
Returns the list of users (students) in the grader report for a given course. Designed for the grader report user search widget.

End an active BigBlueButton meeting session, disconnecting all participants. Requires moderator role in the BBB activity.

Get live status and details of a BigBlueButton meeting, including whether it is running, participant/moderator counts, opening/closing times, join URL, and enabled features.

Trigger the course module viewed event and update the module completion status.

Read (get, fetch) one forum post by its id, with its author, its parent and what you may do to it. Read (list, fetch) every post in one discussion, the whole thread in one call. Return capabilities information for a given forum.

List (browse, find) the discussions in one forum, with their reply and unread counts. Each entry carries only the discussion's FIRST post; read the replies with mod_forum_get_discussion_posts. Returns a list of forum instances in the given courses. If no course IDs are provided, returns all forums the user has access to.
Prepares a draft area for editing a post.
Toggle the lock state of a forum discussion. Locks an unlocked discussion or unlocks a locked one.
Pin or unpin a forum discussion so it appears at the top of the discussion list.
Subscribe or unsubscribe the current user to a specific discussion within a forum.
Star or unstar (favourite/unfavourite) a forum discussion for the current user.

Edit (update, reword, correct, pin) a forum post. Add a new entry to a glossary. In a glossary with defaultapproval off the entry stays hidden until someone with the approve capability approves it.
Delete the given entry from the glossary.
Get the list of authors who have contributed entries to a glossary.
Get the categories defined in a glossary.

Browse glossary entries filtered by author's first or last name initial letter. Requires the glossary display format to support 'author' browse mode, otherwise throws invalidbrowsemode. Definitions come back display-formatted: multilang is collapsed to one language, autolinks are baked in and file references are rewritten to URLs, so never write a definition read here back to the glossary. Read the raw values with x_mod_glossary_entry_pre_update before editing an entry.

Browse glossary entries filtered by a specific author's user ID. Requires the glossary display format to support 'author' browse mode, otherwise throws invalidbrowsemode. Read the raw values with x_mod_glossary_entry_pre_update before editing an entry.

Browse glossary entries filtered by the first letter of the concept. The 'letter' browse mode is always available regardless of glossary display format. Search glossary entries by query string, with optional full-text search. Look up glossary entries by exact concept or alias match. List glossary entries pending approval, filterable by letter. Get a single glossary entry by its ID, including permissions and rating info. Read the raw values with x_mod_glossary_entry_pre_update before editing an entry.
Retrieve a list of glossaries from several courses.

Get total number of the tool types and tool proxies
Check whether a given URL points to an IMS LTI cartridge XML file.

Set whether an LTI tool appears in one course's activity chooser. It works on both kinds: a site tool gets a per-course override, a course tool is changed outright. It does nothing to a tool whose configuration usage is hidden, which is offered nowhere. The tool stays usable by x_mod_lti_create_modules either way; only the chooser changes. Find tool ids with x_mod_lti_get_tool_types.

Update the name, description or state of a site-level LTI tool registration. Only those three fields, and an empty value is ignored rather than clearing the field. Prefer x_mod_lti_update_tool_type, which patches every setting in either scope.
Trigger the course module viewed event and update the module completion status.
Returns a list of Page resource activities in the given courses, including their HTML content. If no course IDs are provided, returns all pages the user can view across their enrolled courses.
Trigger the course module viewed event and update the module completion status for a Page resource.
Add a number of random questions to a quiz.
Create grade items for a quiz, one per section. Throws an exception if the quiz already has grade items.
Create quiz grade items. All grade items must belong to the same quiz.
Delete quiz grade items. The grade items must not be assigned to any quiz slots (questions).
Delete quiz overrides (user or group overrides for dates, time limit, attempts, etc.).
Return access information for the current user's quiz attempt, including whether the quiz is finished, reasons preventing a new attempt, and whether a preflight check (e.g. password) is required.
Return quiz question data for an in-progress attempt. Only works for the current user's own in-progress attempt. Returns rendered HTML, not structured question data.
Return review data for a finished quiz attempt. Can be used by students to review their own attempts or by teachers to review any student's attempt. The attempt must be finished.
Return a summary of the current user's in-progress quiz attempt, showing the status of each question before submitting.
Get the combined review display options across all of a user's attempts at a quiz, indicating which feedback elements (marks, correct answers, feedback, etc.) are visible.
Get the data required to re-render the Quiz grading setup page
Get all date, time limit, attempts, and password overrides for a given quiz, including both user and group overrides.
Return the current user's capabilities and access rule information for a given quiz, including whether they can attempt, manage, preview, review attempts, and view reports.
Get the feedback text that should be show to a student who got the given grade in the given quiz.
Return the list of question type plugin names used in a given quiz, including potential types from random question categories.
Returns a list of quizzes in the given courses with their settings. If no course ids are provided, returns quizzes from all courses the user is enrolled in.
Return an HTML confirmation message for reopening an abandoned quiz attempt. Only works for attempts in the 'abandoned' (never submitted) state.
Return a list of attempts for the given quiz and user.
Get the best current grade for the given user on a quiz.
Submit question responses during an in-progress quiz attempt. Can also be used to finish (submit) the attempt.
Re-open a quiz attempt that is currently in the 'abandoned' (never submitted) state, allowing the student to continue it.
Processes save requests during the quiz.                               This function is intended for the quiz auto-save feature.
Create or update quiz overrides for specific users or groups. Overrides allow changing the quiz open/close time, time limit, number of attempts, or password for individual users or groups.
Set which version of a question to use in a specific quiz slot. Pass 0 or null for 'always use latest version'.
Starts a new attempt at a quiz.
Update the question bank filter condition for a random question slot in a quiz. The filter condition is a JSON-encoded object that determines which questions can be randomly selected.
Rename quiz grade items. All grade items must belong to the same quiz. Only the name property can be updated.
Update the properties of slots in a quiz. All slots must belong to the same quiz.
Trigger the attempt viewed event and update the current page of the attempt. This is for logging purposes in the mobile app.
Trigger the attempt reviewed event. This is for logging purposes in the mobile app.
Trigger the attempt summary viewed event. This is for logging purposes in the mobile app.

Returns file resource activities in the given courses. Each one carries contentfiles, holding the name, size and download URL of every uploaded file; pass a download URL to read_file to read the file itself. If no course IDs are provided, returns resources from all courses the user is enrolled in.
Triggers the course_module_viewed event and marks activity completion for a file resource. Does not return the resource content.
Return capabilities information for a given scorm.
Return the number of attempts done by a user in the given SCORM.
Retrieves SCORM tracking data (scores, completion status, time spent, interactions) for a specific SCO, user, and attempt.
Returns all SCOs (Shareable Content Objects) in a SCORM package, including their titles, launch files, and hierarchy. SCOs are the individual learning objects within a SCORM package.
Retrieves the current user's SCORM tracking data and default SCORM data model values for all SCOs in a SCORM package for a given attempt. Only returns data for the current user.
Returns a list of SCORM activities in the given courses, including settings, grades configuration, and availability. If no courses are provided, returns all SCORM activities the user can access.
Saves SCORM runtime tracking data for the current user. Requires knowledge of SCORM data model element names (e.g. cmi.core.score.raw, cmi.core.lesson_status).
Triggers the SCO launched event and marks the SCORM activity as viewed for completion tracking. Used by the SCORM player to signal that a user has started a SCO.
Triggers the SCORM course module viewed event for logging and completion tracking.
Get the complete list of questions for the survey, including subquestions.
Returns a list of survey instances in a provided set of courses,                               if no courses are provided then all the survey instances the user has access to will be returned.
Submit the answers for a given survey.
Trigger the course module viewed event and update the module completion status.
Returns a list of URL resource activities in the given courses. If no course IDs are provided, returns all URL resources the user can view across their enrolled courses.
Trigger the course module viewed event and update the module completion status.

Update the contents of an existing wiki page, either the whole page or one named section. Releases the editing lock afterwards. Read the current raw markup with mod_wiki_get_page_for_editing first; never write back the rendered HTML returned by mod_wiki_get_page_contents. Fails if another user holds the lock. Attach files by staging them with create_draft_file_area and passing the draft id as attachmentsid; attaching never removes files the other pages use.

Returns the contents of a wiki page by its page ID: the RENDERED HTML, plus title, tags and version number. The rendered HTML is not the page source and must never be written back with mod_wiki_edit_page. To read a page you intend to edit, use mod_wiki_get_page_for_editing, which returns the raw markup.

Locks a wiki page for editing and returns its raw source content, for the whole page or one named section. This is the correct way to read a page before mod_wiki_edit_page: the rendered HTML from mod_wiki_get_page_contents is not the page source and must never be saved back. The lock blocks other users from editing until mod_wiki_edit_page releases it, so call this only when you are about to save.

Returns the list of files attached to a specific subwiki, identified by wiki instance ID and optionally group/user. Files belong to the subwiki, not to one page, so every page shares this list. Each file reports usedincurrentversions, saying whether any page still links to it; unused files stay in place until someone deletes them in the wiki's file manager.
Returns the list of all pages in a wiki, including titles, content, view counts, and modification times. Specify the wiki instance ID; group and user IDs are optional for group/individual wikis.

Returns the list of subwikis the user can see in a specific wiki. In collaborative mode there is one subwiki per group; in individual mode there is one subwiki per user (per group). Use this to discover subwiki IDs needed by other wiki functions.
Returns a list of wiki instances in a provided set of courses, if no courses are provided then all the wiki instances the user has access to will be returned.

Create a new page in a wiki. Provide either a subwikiid, or a wikiid (with optional userid and groupid), in which case the subwiki is created if it does not exist yet, so this also populates a brand new wiki. The page title must be unique within the subwiki. The wiki finds its front page by matching the title against the wiki's firstpagetitle setting, so the first page you create must carry exactly that title or the wiki keeps showing as empty; read it with x_mod_wiki_pre_update. Attach files by staging them with create_draft_file_area and passing the draft id as attachmentsid; attaching never removes files the other pages use.
Trigger the page viewed event and update the module completion status.
Trigger the course module viewed event and update the module completion status.
Add a new submission to a given workshop. Workshop must be in submission phase and user must have assessed all required examples before submitting.
Deletes the given submission.
Evaluates an assessment (used by teachers to provide feedback to the reviewer and optionally override the grading grade).
Evaluates a submission (used by teachers to provide feedback or override the submission grade).
Retrieves the given assessment.
Retrieves the assessment form definition (the grading criteria dimensions, fields, and options used to assess a submission).
Returns the final assessment and submission grades from the gradebook for the given user in a workshop.
Retrieves the workshop grades report showing all participants with their submission grades, assessment grades, and peer review details. Requires mod/workshop:viewallassessments capability.
Retrieves all the assessments reviewed by the given user.
Retrieves the given submission.
Retrieves all the assessments of the given submission.
Retrieves all the workshop submissions or the one done by the given user (except example submissions).
Return the workshop phase/task planner for a user, showing which phases are active and which tasks are completed.
Return the current user's capabilities and permission flags for a given workshop instance (e.g. whether they can submit, assess, view all submissions, etc.).

Returns the workshops in the given courses, or every workshop the user can see when no courses are given, each with its settings and the phase it is in. The strategy field says how assessments are graded: accumulative gives a mark and a comment per criterion, comments gives comments with no marks, numerrors is a yes or no checklist whose failures map to a grade, and rubric has the assessor pick one described level per criterion.
Submit or update a peer assessment for an allocated submission. Requires the assessment form data from get_assessment_form_definition.
Update the given submission.
Trigger the submission viewed event.
Trigger the course module viewed event and update the module completion status.
Takes care of what needs to be done when a PayPal transaction comes back as complete.
Returns the configuration settings to be used in js
Sets the width of columns in the question bank view, either as a user preference or global config.
Sets the display order of columns in the question bank view, either as a user preference or global config.
Sets which columns are hidden in the question bank view, either as a user preference or global config.
Set the status of a question version (Ready or Draft). Requires question edit capability in the question's context.
Move a question bank category to a new parent and/or position within its siblings. Returns reactive state updates for the UI.
Update the question tags.
Sets the current user's preference for how question text is displayed in the question bank (off, plain text, or full HTML).
Validate a Safe Exam Browser config key or a browser exam key.
Read (open, examine, analyse) a file referenced in this conversation: a file the user attached, or a pluginfile URL returned by another tool.
Get token
Returns a user's competency proficiency data for a course, including grades, competency frameworks, and related courses. The user must be enrolled and have the gradable capability.
Records that a user has taken an action (e.g. acknowledged, not useful) on one or more analytics predictions.
Flags a prediction as fixed.
Flags the prediction as not useful.

Resize an image attached to this conversation. Specify target width and/or height in pixels. Set one dimension to 0 to auto-calculate it while maintaining aspect ratio. The resized image is attached to the conversation automatically.
Pause for the given number of seconds. Used by Behat scenarios that exercise the chat UI under observable tool-call delays.
Reset an autosave session
Resume an autosave session
Update an autosave session
Applies Moodle content filters to equation markup (e.g. TeX) for preview in the TinyMCE equation editor.
Get the Tiny Premium API key from Moodle
Delete a custom admin settings preset by ID. Only custom presets can be deleted, not core presets.

Create (add, define) a button placement: where the AI agent button appears (a set of URL masks and a display location) and, optionally, the skills a conversation started from it preloads. Edit it afterwards with tool_adminagent_update_placement.
Create (add, define) a new skill: a block of instructions plus two function masks that scope the tools it brings. Edit it afterwards with tool_adminagent_update_skill.
Delete (remove) a button placement by id.
Delete (remove) a skill by shortname.
Deactivate or re-check the AI agent license and re-render the status block

List the functions the agent can use (web service functions and built-in tools), with each function's name, component, description and tags. This only LISTS functions for reference; unlike search_tools, it does NOT make them available for the agent to call. Use it to choose the masks when configuring a skill, or to browse available functionality.
Enable, disable, delete or duplicate AI agent button placements

Fetch (read, get) an existing placement's current fields before editing it. Returns the name, URL masks, location, pinned skill shortnames and welcome text so you can modify them and pass them to tool_adminagent_update_placement (which replaces the URL masks and skills wholesale).

List (search, find, browse) the button placements, each with its id, name, location, URL masks, pinned skill shortnames and enabled state. Use it to find a placement's id before editing it; fetch the full record with tool_adminagent_placement_pre_update.

List (search, find, browse) the configured skills, each with its shortname, name, description and enabled state. Use it to discover which skills exist before editing one; fetch a skill's full definition (instructions and function masks) with tool_adminagent_skill_pre_update.
Bulk enable or disable AI agent functions
Preview or import AI agent skills

Fetch (read, get) an existing skill's current fields before editing it. Returns name, description, instructions and the functions masks so you can modify them and pass them to tool_adminagent_update_skill (which replaces the mask arrays wholesale).

Edit (update, rename, move, enable, disable, re-target) an existing button placement by id. Only the fields you pass are changed. Call tool_adminagent_placement_pre_update first to read the current values — the URL masks and skills are replaced wholesale, not merged.

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, enable, disable, reconfigure the functions of) an existing skill by shortname. Only the fields you pass are changed. Call tool_adminagent_skill_pre_update first to read the current values — the functions arrays are replaced wholesale, not merged.
Search for contexts (courses, categories, etc.) that can be used to restrict an analytics model. Used in the analytics model configuration UI.
Get the required fields for a Behat data generator entity type (e.g. 'users', 'courses'). Only works in development environments with Behat installed.
Approve a pending GDPR data request (data export or deletion request) for a user.
Bulk approve multiple pending GDPR data requests (data export or deletion requests).
Bulk deny multiple pending GDPR data requests (data export or deletion requests).
Cancel a pending GDPR data request. The current user can only cancel their own requests or requests they created on behalf of another user.
Approve expired data retention contexts for deletion. This confirms that the data in these contexts can be purged as part of the GDPR data retention policy.
Send a message to the site Data Protection Officer(s). Creates a general enquiry data request and notifies each DPO via message.
Create a GDPR data category for classifying types of personal data (e.g. 'Contact information', 'Academic records'). Requires serialised Moodle form data.
Create a GDPR data request for data export or deletion. Type 1 = export personal data, type 2 = delete personal data. Can be created for the current user or on behalf of another user if permitted.
Create a GDPR data purpose defining why personal data is collected and its retention period. Requires serialised Moodle form data.
Delete a GDPR data category used for classifying types of personal data.
Delete a GDPR data purpose that defines why personal data is collected and its retention period.
Deny a pending GDPR data request (data export or deletion request) for a user.
Get the current user's GDPR/privacy permissions and status: whether they can contact the DPO, manage data requests, create export/deletion requests, and whether they have ongoing requests.
Fetches a list of activity module plugins available for setting data registry defaults. Optionally filters to only activities without existing defaults.
Fetches a list of data category options
Fetch the details of a user's data request
Fetches data privacy requests with optional filtering by user, status, type, and creation method. Users can view their own requests; DPOs can view all requests.
Fetches a list of data storage purpose options
Searches for users by name (prefix match) for data privacy request management. Excludes admin and guest users. Returns up to 30 results.
Mark a data privacy general enquiry request as complete. Only applies to requests that are general enquiries (not export or deletion requests).
Updates the default category and purpose for a given context level (and optionally, a plugin)
Sets purpose and category for a specific context
Sets purpose and category across a context level
Approves a data export request with an optional filter to include only selected courses. Requires submitting serialised Moodle form data.
Returns child branches (courses, modules, or blocks) for a given context in the data registry tree. Used to expand the data registry navigation tree.
Load the data for the competencies manage page template
Load the data for the competency frameworks manage page template
Load a summary of a competency, including optionally related competencies and linked courses.
Load the data for the course competencies page template.
Load the data for a single learning plan, including its competencies and user proficiency status.
Load all learning plans for a user.
Load the data for the related competencies template.
Load a learning plan template with its linked competencies and statistics.
Load the data for the learning plan templates manage page template
Load a summary of a user competency.
Load a summary of a user competency within the context of a specific course.
Load a summary of a user competency within the context of a specific learning plan.
Load all evidence of prior learning for a user.
Load a single evidence of prior learning record.
List the courses using a competency
Search for cohorts. This method is deprecated, please call 'core_cohort_search_cohorts' instead
Search for users who have a specific capability, filtered for use in learning plan template management.
Call multiple external functions and return all responses.

Creates an auto-login key for the current user.                               Is created only in https sites and is restricted by time, ip address and only works if the request                               comes from the Moodle mobile or desktop app.

Returns site configuration settings as name-value pairs, optionally filtered by section. Sections include: frontpagesettings, sitepolicies, gradessettings, mobileapp, calendar, coursecolors, supportcontact, graceperiodsettings, navigation, themesettings, locationsettings, manageglobalsearch, privacysettings, blog, h5psettings. Some admin-only settings require moodle/site:config.
Returns a piece of content to be displayed in the Mobile app.
Returns a list of Moodle plugins supporting the mobile app.
Returns a list of the site public settings, those not requiring authentication.
Returns a WebService token (and private token) for QR login.
Check if the given site subscription key is valid.
Search for courses by name where the current user has the capability to manage activities. Returns course id, name, category, and image. Designed for MoodleNet content import.
Verify if the passed information resolves into a WebFinger profile URL
Fetch the details of a policy version
Get all policies and their acceptance status for a user, including policy content, acceptance details, and action permissions.
Set the acceptance status (accept or decline only) for the indicated policies for the given user.
Accept policies on behalf of other users
Send test events for the test settings page
List/search templates by component.
Load a canonical template by name (not the theme overidden one).
Mark the specified tour as completed for the current user
Fetch the specified tour
Reset the specified tour so it will be shown again to the current user
Mark the specified tour step as shown for the current user (fires a step_shown event)
Reorders database schema elements (tables, fields, keys, indexes) in the XMLDB editor by moving them up or down.

Read (get, inspect) the access restrictions (availability conditions) on an activity (cmid) or course section (sectionid) before editing them with x_core_availability_update. Pass either id, not both. Returns: availability (the raw restriction tree as a JSON string, or null when unrestricted; send it back to x_core_availability_update with your changes applied, since the whole tree is replaced); summary (plain-text rendering of the current restrictions); enabled_availability_plugins (condition type names usable on this site); available_profile_fields (standard and custom user profile field shortnames usable in a profile condition). Load the availability_restrictions skill for the tree grammar and condition fields.
Set, add, change or remove access restrictions (availability conditions) on an activity or course section. Pass the tree as JSON in availabilityjson; empty string clears all restrictions.
Find (list, show, browse) a course's backups in order to download one, analyse what it contains, or extract its data in full or in part; extract_files unpacks the .mbz archive.

Read (get, inspect) a course's completion criteria and aggregation before editing them. This is COURSE completion (the overall requirements to complete the course), NOT per-activity completion conditions. Returns the criteria (activities, prerequisite courses, date, enrolment duration, grade, self completion, roles) keyed exactly as x_core_completion_course_update accepts, each aggregation as all/any, human-readable criteria_titles, the valid values for the update tool's inputs (available_activities_cmids = course modules with completion enabled, for activities_cmids; available_roleids = roles that can mark a student complete, for roleids), the lock state (locked, completed_user_data_count), and warnings to resolve or note before editing (the settings being locked by existing user completion data, completion turned off, or a criterion referencing a deleted or misconfigured activity, course or role). Edit them with x_core_completion_course_update.

Set (configure, change, clear) a course's completion criteria: completion by activities, prerequisite courses, a date, an enrolment duration, a course grade, self completion, or a role marking the student complete, and how they combine. This is COURSE completion, not the per-activity completion conditions set on individual activities.
Create (author, build) new H5P content in the content bank from an installed content type, without uploading a package. List the content types with x_core_contentbank_get_content_types first.
List (find) the H5P content types installed on this site, with the library name each one needs. Call this before x_core_contentbank_create_h5p_content, which cannot be used without a library name.
List (browse, search, find) content bank items and their ids. This is where the ids come from for adding an H5P activity and for every content bank function that takes a contentid.

Upload (add, import) a file into the content bank, or replace the file of an item already there. Which file types are accepted depends on the content type plugins installed, which on a stock site means .h5p packages and nothing else; any other file is refused. To build H5P content without a package file, use x_core_contentbank_create_h5p_content.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a course category before editing it: name, description, idnumber, parent and theme, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields keyed as core_course_update_categories accepts. Visibility is reported for context but is read-only here.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a course before editing it: full name, short name, summary, format and the format's current option keys, plus visibility, dates and category, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields keyed as core_course_update_courses accepts. The courseformatoptions returned are the valid option keys for this course's format, so use those exact names rather than inventing option keys.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a course section before editing it: name, summary, visibility and access restrictions, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same shape x_core_courseformat_update_section accepts. A null name means the section shows its default generated name (for example "Topic 1").

Update a course section's name, description, or visibility. Pass the section ID (obtained from core_course_get_contents) and the fields to update. Before changing the name or description, call x_core_courseformat_section_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Read the full advanced grading state of an activity's grading area before editing it with core_grading_save_definitions: ALL stored grading form definitions (drafts and forms of inactive methods included; a form survives switching to another method and resurfaces when switched back), each with its raw description, method options and criteria exactly as core_grading_save_definitions accepts them. Returns: areaname; activemethod ('' = simple direct grading); simple_grading_fallback (true = the active method's form is missing or a draft, so simple direct grading is silently used, as the UI warns); definable_methods (methods whose forms these functions can save); ui_only_methods (installed methods whose forms are edited in the UI only); definitions, each with method, id, name, status (10 = draft, 20 = ready), description (raw), descriptionformat, has_graded_instances (true = editing prompts regrading of existing grades) and the method's form content, options included, keyed exactly as core_grading_save_definitions accepts it.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) a group's current state before editing it: name, description, enrolment key, visibility, participation, messaging, picture and every custom field the site defines, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields keyed as core_group_update_groups accepts.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) a grouping's current state before editing it: name, idnumber, description and every custom field the site defines, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields keyed as core_group_update_groupings accepts.
List the roles the current user is allowed to assign in a given context. Use this BEFORE calling core_role_assign_roles so you pick a roleid that is valid.

Create one or more 'assign' activities in a Moodle course. Assignments collect student work (online text, file uploads, or both), grade it, and let teachers leave feedback. Supports group submissions, deadlines, marking workflows, and submission/feedback subplugins.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of an Assignment before editing it: name, intro, activity instructions, dates, submission/feedback types, grading and marking options, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_assign_update_module accepts. The locked_fields array names settings the update tool refuses to change once submissions or grades exist (for example blindmarking).

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'assign' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_assign_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.
Create one or more 'bigbluebuttonbn' activities in a Moodle course. A BigBlueButton activity is a live online meeting room inside the course, optionally with recordings.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a BigBlueButton activity before editing it: name, intro, room, recording, guest-access and schedule settings, as they are stored, without filters. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_bigbluebuttonbn_update_module accepts, plus an introfiles listing and presentationfiles, the one pre-uploaded presentation file.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'bigbluebuttonbn' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_bigbluebuttonbn_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) a Book's chapters before editing: title and HTML body as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing, plus each chapter's embedded-file listing with a warning for files the body no longer references. Returns fields in the same shape x_mod_book_update_chapter accepts.
Add (create, append, insert) one or more chapters or subchapters in a Book activity, with HTML body content.

Create one or more 'book' activities in a Moodle course. A Book is a multi-page resource organised into chapters and subchapters with a generated table of contents — ideal for long-form course material. Creating a book produces an empty shell; use x_mod_book_create_chapters afterwards to add reading content.
Delete (remove) one or more chapters from a Book activity. Multiple chapters can be deleted in one call. The 'subchapters' parameter controls what happens to nested chapters of a deleted parent.
List (read, view) the chapters of a Book activity: its table of contents in display order, with parentchapterid resolved for each subchapter. Optionally returns chapters contents.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Book activity before editing it: name, intro and the book settings (numbering, custom titles), as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_book_update_module accepts. Chapter content is handled separately: read it with x_mod_book_chapter_pre_update and edit it with x_mod_book_update_chapter.

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, hide, move, reorder) an existing chapter in a Book activity. Change its title, HTML body, visibility, and/or its position. Only the fields you pass are changed. Before changing the title or body, call x_mod_book_chapter_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'book' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_book_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.
Create one or more 'choice' activities in a Moodle course. A choice asks participants one question with a fixed set of options, and can show the results back to them.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Choice activity before editing it: name, intro, settings and every option with its id, cap and response count, as they are stored, without filters. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_choice_update_module accepts, plus has_answers, which is 1 when allowmultiple is frozen because participants have already answered.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'choice' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_choice_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Add (create, define) fields to a Database activity, as one all-or-nothing batch: every field is validated first and nothing is created when any of them fails. Fields display in creation order and cannot be reordered later, so send them together in their final order; call x_mod_data_pre_update first when the database may already have fields. Load the mod_data_management skill for the per-type param meanings.

Create one or more 'data' activities in a Moodle course. A database collects structured entries that participants fill in through teacher-defined fields such as text, numbers, menus, dates, files and images. A new database has no fields; define them with x_mod_data_create_fields before adding entries. Load the mod_data_management skill for the whole workflow.

Delete (remove, drop) one field from a Database activity. Everything entries hold in that field is deleted with it, and deleting the last remaining field of a database that still has entries deletes all of those entries too.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Database activity before editing it: name, intro, entry and approval settings as x_mod_data_update_module accepts them, the field list with raw paramN settings (the same vocabulary the field tools take), templates_overridden (which template columns hold custom content; contents via x_mod_data_templates_pre_update) and entries_count, all raw and unfiltered.

Read (get, inspect) a Database activity's ten display templates before editing them with x_mod_data_update_templates. Returns, per template: current (the raw stored value), isoverridden (whether a custom value is stored), default (what a reset would regenerate from the current fields; empty while the database has no fields), and placeholders (the field and ##action## tags usable in that template). Load the mod_data_management skill for the template syntax.

Edit (update, rename, reconfigure) one field of a Database activity: its name, description, whether it is required, and its raw param settings. Only the properties you pass are changed. A field's type cannot be changed; delete it and create a new one instead. Call x_mod_data_pre_update first to read the current values; load the mod_data_management skill for the per-type param meanings.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'data' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_data_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Edit (set, override) or reset the display templates of a Database activity: the entry list, single entry view, add entry form, advanced search form, RSS feed, CSS and JavaScript. Call x_mod_data_templates_pre_update first for the current values, the defaults and the placeholders each template accepts. A reset template regenerates its default automatically once the database has fields. Load the mod_data_management skill for the template tag syntax.
Add (create, insert) questions, headings and page breaks to a Feedback activity.
Create one or more 'feedback' activities in a Moodle course. A feedback is a survey of your own questions. A new one has no questions; add them with x_mod_feedback_create_items.
Delete (remove) one question, heading or page break from a Feedback activity. Answers already given to that question are deleted with it, and the remaining items close the gap.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Feedback activity before editing it: name, intro and the survey settings as x_mod_feedback_update_module accepts them, all raw and unfiltered; has_responses, which is 1 once anyone has answered; and items, every question, heading and page break in order, with its position, page and settings in the same vocabulary x_mod_feedback_update_item accepts. Read this before editing, moving or deleting a question: no core function returns a question's settings in a form you can write back.
Edit (change, rename, reword, move, reorder) one question, heading or page break of a Feedback activity. Read it with x_mod_feedback_pre_update first. The question type cannot be changed.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'feedback' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_feedback_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.
Create one or more 'folder' activities in a Moodle course. A Folder displays a set of related files in one place, either as an inline list or a downloadable folder.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Folder activity before editing it: name, intro, the folder's file tree (with paths) and display settings, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_folder_update_module accepts; use the listed file paths before add or replace operations.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'folder' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_folder_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Create one or more 'forum' activities in a Moodle course. Forums are asynchronous discussion areas where teachers and students post messages, reply in threads, and subscribe to receive updates by email. Forum types include standard, single-discussion, each-person-posts-one, Q&A, and blog-like.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) one forum post before editing it: subject and message exactly as stored, with the stored message format. Every read web service formats the message instead, so this is the only lossless way to read a post you intend to write back with mod_forum_update_discussion_post.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Forum activity before editing it: name, intro, forum type, subscription and read-tracking modes, dates, attachment and moderation settings, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_forum_update_module accepts.
Search (find, look up) forum posts the way the forum advanced search page does: words, exact phrase, excluded words, subject, author, date range, tags and starred discussions.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'forum' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_forum_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Add (create) one or more categories in a glossary, so entries can be grouped and browsed by category. List the existing ones with mod_glossary_get_categories; assign entries to them with the categories option of mod_glossary_add_entry.

Create one or more 'glossary' activities in a Moodle course. A glossary is a list of concepts and definitions that participants can browse, search and (with permission) add entries to. Entries are added afterwards with mod_glossary_add_entry.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) one glossary entry before editing it: concept, definition, aliases, categories and linking flags exactly as stored, without filters or file post-processing. Every read web service formats the definition, so this is the only lossless way to read an entry you intend to write back with mod_glossary_update_entry.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Glossary activity before editing it: name, intro, entry and appearance settings, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_glossary_update_module accepts, plus an introfiles listing and has_main_glossary_conflict, which is 1 when another main glossary in the course freezes mainglossary to 0.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'glossary' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_glossary_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Setting defaultapproval to 1 immediately approves every entry in the glossary that is still awaiting approval.

Create one or more 'h5pactivity' activities in a Moodle course. An H5P activity plays interactive content from an uploaded .h5p package or from a content bank item, one of which is required. Find content bank items with x_core_contentbank_search_contents.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of an H5P activity before editing it: name, intro, display, tracking and grading settings, as they are stored, without filters. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_h5pactivity_update_module accepts, plus packagefiles (the .h5p file the activity currently plays), islinkedtocontentbank, which is 1 when the activity follows a content bank item rather than holding its own copy, and has_attempts, a caution flag that students have already played it.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'h5pactivity' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_h5pactivity_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Create one or more 'label' activities in a Moodle course. A Text and Media area (formerly 'label') displays HTML/text inline on the course page — the 'intro' field IS the content. Use to add headings, instructions, embedded media, or any inline content between activities. The 'name' is optional and only used in course navigation.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Text and Media area (label) before editing it. Its content IS the intro field, returned as it is stored, without filters or file post-processing, plus visibility and the intro file listing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_label_update_module accepts.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'label' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_label_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Add (create, append, insert) one or more cluster start pages to a Lesson. A cluster marks the start of a randomised pool of pages — between the cluster and the next endofcluster page, students see a random subset rather than every page in order. Useful for "show N random questions out of M" quizzes within a lesson. The pool pages should use jumpto "cluster_jump" on their answers so the runtime routes back into the pool. Pair with x_mod_lesson_create_endofcluster_pages to close the cluster.

Add (create, append, insert) one or more content / branchtable pages to a Lesson activity. Each page has an HTML body plus a list of branches (buttons) that jump to other pages. Use jumpto "endbranch" on any branch and the tool will auto-create a shared endofbranch page at the end of the batch — useful for closing simple branching scenarios in one call without managing the endofbranch row explicitly. Position via beforepageid (omit to append).

Add (create, append, insert) one or more endofcluster pages to a Lesson. An endofcluster page closes a randomised pool of pages started by a cluster page. See x_mod_lesson_create_cluster_pages for the build pattern.

Add (create, append, insert) one or more essay pages to a Lesson activity. The student writes a free-form response; grading is manual by the teacher. Each page just carries the post-essay jumpto + an optional max score.

Add (create, append, insert) one or more matching question pages to a Lesson. The student pairs each stem with its correct match from a dropdown. Provide pairs[] plus page-level correct_jumpto / wrong_jumpto. At least 2 pairs required.

Create one or more 'lesson' activities in a Moodle course. A Lesson is a branching activity built from content / question pages connected by jumps. After creation the lesson is empty — add pages with x_mod_lesson_create_*_pages (separate tools) to populate it.

Add (create, append, insert) one or more multichoice question pages to a Lesson activity. The student picks an answer; correct ones advance to the next page, wrong ones keep them on the same page to retry. Set multianswer=true on a page to require selecting ALL correct answers. Position via beforepageid (omit to append). Use score for custom scoring.

Add (create, append, insert) one or more numerical question pages to a Lesson. The student types a number; the runtime matches against listed answer values or ranges and routes by the matching row's jumpto. Answer text is a number ("42") or a colon-separated range ("40:50"). Use other_answers_jumpto for the catch-all.

Add (create, append, insert) one or more shortanswer question pages to a Lesson. The student types a short text response; the runtime matches against the listed answers (case-insensitive by default, with * wildcards) and routes by the matching row's jumpto. Use other_answers_jumpto for the catch-all when nothing matches.
Add (create, append, insert) one or more true/false question pages to a Lesson activity. Exactly 2 answers per page. Position via beforepageid (omit to append).

Delete (remove, drop) one or more pages from a Lesson activity. Works for any page type. Other pages' jumpto references are NOT auto-rewritten — call x_mod_lesson_pre_update afterwards to see any newly-broken jumpto warnings, then repair them with the update tool.

Read (get, fetch, inspect, audit) the current state of a Lesson activity — settings, pages, branches, navigation flow, answer text, attached files, and integrity warnings. Text fields come back exactly as stored (no language filters, no autolink, no formatters), so this is the source of truth before any x_mod_lesson_update_* call. Structural warnings flag orphaned pages, broken jumpto refs, branchtables missing an endofbranch, and lesson-level cross-field conflicts.

Edit (update, rename) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single cluster start page. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed.

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, hide) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single branchtable / content page in a Lesson. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed. Providing branches REPLACES the existing branch list — include unchanged branches if you want them to stay.

Edit (update, rename) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single endofcluster page. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed.

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, hide) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single essay page. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed.

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, hide) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single matching question page. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed. Providing pairs REPLACES the existing pairs. correct_jumpto / wrong_jumpto / correct_score / wrong_score / *_response can be sent independently (they update the master rows even without new pairs).

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'lesson' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_lesson_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, hide) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single multichoice question page. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed. Providing answers REPLACES the existing answer list.

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, hide) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single numerical page. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed. Providing answers REPLACES the existing answer list (plus catch-all if other_answers_jumpto is also set).

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, hide) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single shortanswer page. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed. Providing answers REPLACES the existing answer list (plus catch-all if other_answers_jumpto is also set).

Edit (update, rename, rewrite, hide) OR MOVE / REORDER an EXISTING single true/false question page. Use this tool to reposition a page within its lesson — set beforepageid to the id of the page it should sit before. Only the fields you send are changed. Providing answers REPLACES the existing answers (still must be exactly 2).

Create one or more 'lti' activities in a Moodle course. An External Tool activity launches a preconfigured LTI tool. Find the typeid to use with x_mod_lti_get_tool_types; if the tool you need is not registered yet, register it with x_mod_lti_create_tool_types first.
Register (add, configure) external tools (LTI) so teachers can add activities that launch them. Check x_mod_lti_get_tool_types first: registering a launch URL twice is allowed but rarely wanted.
List (find, discover) the external tools (LTI) registered on this site, with the typeid each needs. Call before x_mod_lti_create_modules, which cannot work without one, and before registering a tool.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of an External tool activity before editing it: name, intro, launch appearance, privacy choices and grading settings as x_mod_lti_update_module accepts them, all raw and unfiltered, plus locked_fields, holding the typeid of the tool this activity launches and that tool's name. The launched tool is fixed at creation and cannot be changed by an update.

Read (get, inspect) a registered external tool's (LTI) current settings before x_mod_lti_update_tool_type, exactly as stored. The shared secret and any private key are replaced with a placeholder and keep their stored values unless you send new ones.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'lti' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_lti_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Change (edit, patch, reconfigure) a registered external tool (LTI). Only the fields you send are changed. Read the current settings with x_mod_lti_tool_type_pre_update first; the shared secret and private key are never returned, and keep their stored values unless you send new ones.
Create one or more 'page' activities in a Moodle course. A Page resource displays HTML content on a single page within the course.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Page activity before editing it: name, intro, content, display settings and attached files, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_page_update_module accepts, plus introfiles and contentfiles listings that flag files the HTML no longer references.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'page' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_page_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.
Add existing question bank questions to a quiz. Questions must already exist in the question bank — use a *_create_questions tool first.

Create one or more 'quiz' activities in a Moodle course. Quizzes are timed assessments built from question-bank questions, with configurable attempt limits, grading methods, feedback rules, and question shuffling. Creating a quiz produces an empty shell — use x_mod_quiz_add_questions afterwards to populate it.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Quiz before editing it: name, intro, timing, attempt and grading settings, and the overall-feedback bands, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_quiz_update_module accepts. has_attempts flags that students have already attempted the quiz, so grading or timing changes may affect existing attempts.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'quiz' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_quiz_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Create one or more 'resource' activities in a Moodle course. A File resource exposes a single uploaded file (PDF, document, image, etc.) for students to view inline or download. A set of related files with one main file is also supported.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a File (resource) activity before editing it: name, intro, the stored file listing and display settings, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_resource_update_module accepts.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'resource' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_resource_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Create one or more 'scorm' activities in a Moodle course. A SCORM activity plays a packaged e-learning course (a SCORM or AICC zip) and records what each student did. Only uploaded packages are supported here; externally hosted ones are not.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a SCORM activity before editing it: name, intro, appearance, availability, grading and attempt settings, as they are stored, without filters. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_scorm_update_module accepts, plus packagefiles (the uploaded package) and has_attempts, a caution flag that students have already attempted it.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'scorm' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_scorm_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Create one or more 'subsection' activities in a Moodle course. A subsection is a collapsible sub-area of a course section that other activities can be moved into. Edit or move the created subsection with the section functions (x_core_courseformat_update_section); delete it like any activity.

Create one or more 'url' activities in a Moodle course. A URL resource links to an external web page or resource. Can be embedded inline in the course page, displayed as a clickable link, or opened in a popup window.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a URL activity before editing it: name, intro, external URL, display settings and query parameters, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_url_update_module accepts.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'url' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_url_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Create one or more 'wiki' activities in a Moodle course. A wiki is a set of pages participants build together, or one private set of pages each. The wiki starts empty; create its first page with mod_wiki_new_page using the exact firstpagetitle as the title.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Wiki activity before editing it: name, intro and format settings, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same flat shape x_mod_wiki_update_module accepts, plus locked_fields carrying wikimode and firstpagetitle, which cannot be changed once the wiki exists.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'wiki' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_wiki_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Add (create, upload) example submissions to a Workshop: sample work students practise assessing before they assess each other. Each one needs a reference assessment afterwards, set with x_mod_workshop_update_example_assessment, or it teaches nothing.

Create one or more 'workshop' activities in a Moodle course. A workshop is peer assessment: students submit work, then assess each other's against a form you define. A new one starts in the setup phase with no assessment form; define one with x_mod_workshop_update_grading_form. Load the mod_workshop_management skill for the whole workflow.
Delete (remove) one example submission from a Workshop. Its reference assessment goes with it, and so does every practice assessment students have already made against it.

Read (get, list, inspect) a Workshop's example submissions and their reference assessments, exactly as the example tools accept them back. The core submission readers leave examples out entirely. Call this before editing, assessing or deleting one.

Read (get, inspect, list) a Workshop's assessment form: its grading strategy and every criterion, exactly as x_mod_workshop_update_grading_form accepts them back. No core function returns them. Call this before editing the form or setting a reference assessment.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a Workshop activity before editing it: name, the four instruction editors with their inline files, and every submission, assessment and grading setting as x_mod_workshop_update_module accepts them, all raw and unfiltered. Also returns phase, the phase the workshop is in; readiness, what the workshop page still lists as outstanding; and has_submissions, has_examples and has_assessments, each of which makes some edits destructive.

Move (switch, advance, reopen) a Workshop to another phase, which is what decides whether students can submit, assess, or only look. Switching does not wait for the current phase to be finished, it reports what was left unfinished.
Edit (change, rename, replace the content of) one example submission of a Workshop. Read it with x_mod_workshop_example_pre_update first. Anything left out keeps what it has, files included.

Set (write, correct) the reference assessment of an example submission: the marks students' practice assessments are compared against. Every criterion of the assessment form has to be marked. Read the criteria with x_mod_workshop_grading_form_pre_update first.

Define or edit (change, replace, set up) the assessment form of a Workshop: the criteria students grade each other against. Read the current form with x_mod_workshop_grading_form_pre_update first. Which properties a criterion takes depends on the workshop's grading strategy.

Edit (update, rename, reschedule, hide, configure) an existing 'workshop' activity. Before changing text fields, call x_mod_workshop_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.

Create one or more 'multichoice' questions in the Moodle question bank. Specify a question category by ID, or provide contextlevel + instanceid (50 + courseid, or 70 + cmid) to use the default category.

Read (get, fetch, inspect) the current state of a multiple-choice question before editing it: question text, general feedback, each answer's text/fraction/feedback, and the combined feedback, as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing. Returns fields in the same shape x_qtype_multichoice_update_question accepts.

Update a 'multichoice' question in the question bank. Before changing text fields, call x_qtype_multichoice_pre_update to read the current values as they are stored, without filters or file post-processing.
